bandReport.notes:
Covers items 21-40, contiguous, no gaps and no repeats. Page-to-item map (0-based PDF index / printed booklet page label): p06 = printed 13, items 21,22,23,24 in c1 and 25,26,27 in c2; p07 = printed 15, items 28,29,30 in c1 and 31,32 in c2; p08 = printed 17, items 33,34 in c1 and 35,36,37 in c2; p09 = printed 19, items 38,39 in c1 and 40 in c2. Item 21 opens with its own number at the top of p06-c1 and item 40's options close well above the foot of p09-c2, so nothing spills into or out of the neighbouring bands. Every item is entirely inside one column - no question straddles the gutter anywhere in this band.

COLUMN SPLIT DEFECT, SYSTEMATIC ON ALL FOUR PAGES: the detected gutter sits a few millimetres to the RIGHT of the right column's item numbers, so every c1 crop ends with the bare item numbers belonging to c2, and every c2 crop opens with un-numbered stems. Specifically p06-c1 carries a trailing '25.', '26.', '27.'; p07-c1 carries '31.', '32.'; p08-c1 carries '35.', '36.', '37.'; p09-c1 carries '40.' (and on p09 the split cuts through the glyphs, leaving '40' at the right edge of c1 and a partial 'l0.' at the left edge of c2). No TEXT was lost or duplicated - only the numerals sit on the wrong side. Each page was checked against pNN.png and every stray number aligns vertically with exactly one c2 stem, so the numbering is unambiguous; c2 items are numbered here from that verified alignment. Reading order used was still all of c1 then all of c2.

The booklet prints Web 3.0 with a raised/middle dot as the decimal separator (Web 3·0). Item 32 is transcribed as printed, per the sibling-band precedent; a reader searching for the string 'Web 3.0' will not match it.

This scan carries a lot of pepper noise. Two specks look like printed characters at low magnification and are NOT transcribed, having been checked at 4x: a full-stop-sized speck immediately before 'Which' in item 23's stem, and one before 'Pennar' in item 24 option (c). Likewise item 21's 'source' images as 'squrce' at page resolution and item 33's 'following' as 'fol!owing'; both are broken glyphs and are transcribed as the real words. Faint Devanagari showing through on several pages is bleed-through from the reverse (Hindi) side, not content of these pages.

Item 28 statement 3 genuinely prints the redundant 'in the entire Indian coastal sands in India' - preserved verbatim. Item 30 pair 4 genuinely pairs Sasthamkotta Lake with Tamil Nadu; that item asks how many pairs are correctly matched, so an incorrect pair is expected content, not a transcription slip. Both items 25 and 30 print a real two-column grid with italic headers and em-dash separators, rendered here as GFM pipe tables with the row numbers kept in the first cell, following the convention already in 2021-p1.b2.
